text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Four days of official talks between Pakistan and the IMF concluded in Washington on Friday without any agreement on stalled releases from a $600 million standby loan.
- Nine Pakistan-owned F-16 jet fighters, now parked in Arizona, will be sold to Indonesia early next year by the United States, the Clinton adminsitration reaffirmed on Thursday.

- President Farooq Leghari, who is on a three-day official visit to Uzbekistan, is likely to meet Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic movement leader Mullah Mohammad Omar and northern warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum there.
- A major investment group of Saudi Arabia, Xenel Industries Ltd, has planned large-scale invesments in various infrastructure development projects in Pakistan.

- Pakistan needs an additional 45 to 50 billion rupees annually to modestly run its day-to-day financial affairs, and studies by both the Central Board of Revenue and the world Bank have advised the government to find new resources by recovering agriculture income tax and detecting tax evaders.
- Yielding to rising pressure at home as well as abroad, the chief ministers of all the four provinces of Pakistan have agreed to tax the income of feudals.

- The formation of a six-member commission to identify big defaulters of loans taken from banks and other financal institutions three years after their names had been published by the caretaker government of Moeen Qureshi shows little hope the federal cabinet has in recovering much of the defaulted 100 billion rupees.
THE NEWS

- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, in an interview with The News, rejected preconditions for talks with opposition parties but showed her readiness for a quid pro quo with them and said opposition leader Nawaz Sharif might make "such a tempting offer" that her government might think of having a four-year term rather than full five years. But she said she was committed to completing her term and holding elections in 1998.
- Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund are believed to have reached a broad understanding on a modified package of reforms approved by the federal cabinet last week.

- Prime Minister's economic affairs adviser V.A. Jafarey said in an interview with The News that Pakistan was in no danger of an economic collapse even if the IMF did not release the stalled standby loan, adding that the government was keen for an edorsement of its policies by the IMF rather than any amount of money.
- The Pakistani government has decided in principle to place a cut on the release of money to its departments to avoid taking more overdrafts to meet current expenditure.
THE NATION

- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, in reply to a letter from President Farooq Leghari, has said her government has decided to strengthen rules and regulations that can help depoliticise the administrative machinery.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The net outflow of foreign investment from the local bourses during September amounted to nearly $20 million owing to an uncertain economic situation and the delay in the release of funds from the IMF.

- Seventeen mutual funds of Investment Corporation of Pakistan were heavily undersubscribed by an average 45 percent as against the total right offers worth 660 million rupees. The funds received around 372.236 million rupees.
- The support price for the procurement of rice for the current 1996-97 season is likely to be raised by the government in the cabinet meeting to be held in Islamabad on Monday.

- The Ministry of Communications has agreed in principle to a proposal of the National Shipowners Association that the import duty on Pakistan flag vessels should be charged only when they are taken to Gaddani for breaking.

- The devaluation of the rupee has put a heavy burden on the national exchequer as the import of petroleum products in term of value has risen by about 60 percent during the third quarter (July-September) of 1996 compared to the corresponding period in 1995.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
